reason: While the text mentions service/worship of God (תַּֽעַבְדוּן - ta'avduun, 'they shall serve/worship'), this passage is primarily concerned with God's identity (as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob), his awareness of Israel's suffering in Egypt, and his commission to Moses to liberate the Israelites. The worship mentioned appears incidental to the main narrative—God says the people will serve him on this mountain, but this is presented as a sign and promise rather than as a statement of what is important to Yahweh. Critically, there is no mention of sacrifice (קרבן/זבח) anywhere in this text. The passage focuses on divine action and human liberation rather than on cultic practices or worship requirements.
